title: Quantum capacity of higher-dimensional depolarizing channels
source: The supplied note derives this question from Hayashi's treatment of quantum capacity. Etxezarreta Martinez, deMarti iOlius, and Crespo explicitly state the unresolved capacity problem for the finite-dimensional depolarizing family in Section~I, p.~2, and define the channel in Section~II, Eq.~(3) \sourcecite{ref:h14-emc}{EMC23}. Their replacement-noise parameter is $p=1-\lambda$.
progress: Kianvash, Fanizza, and Giovannetti construct degradable flagged extensions giving improved upper bounds for qudit depolarizing channels. Their Section~5.4 and Figure~2 include a nontrivial dimension-four comparison; optimizing these extension bounds does not supply matching transmission codes \sourcecite{ref:h14-kfg}{KFG22}.

In the limit of increasing dimension, the no-cloning and hashing bounds meet after division by $\log_2 d$: for fixed $p$, the normalized capacity tends to $\max\{0,1-2p\}$. Theorem~1 and Corollary~1 analyze this normalized gap. This asymptotic statement neither evaluates the capacity for a fixed finite $d\geq3$ nor proves that the absolute gap in qubits vanishes \sourcecite{ref:h14-emc}{EMC23}.

Harish Santhanalakshmi Ganesan evaluated one use of the qutrit channel on $\sigma_2=P_2/2$, where $P_2$ projects onto a two-dimensional subspace. At replacement probability $p=1-\lambda=0.2910672$, this input has coherent information $9.2409\times10^{-8}$ bits per use, while the maximally mixed input $I_3/3$ gives approximately $-0.0160351$ bits. The coding theorem in Eq.~\eqref{eq:h14-capacity} therefore gives strictly positive unassisted quantum capacity at this noise level. The rank-two input remains positive for $0\leq p<p_2(3)$, where its coherent information vanishes at $p_2(3)\approx0.2910672360$. The maximally mixed input reaches zero at $p_{\mathrm h}(3)\approx0.2870866652$. The note also reports that the rank-two input beats the hashing bound on a noise interval for every $3\leq d\leq64$. \sourcecite{ref:h14-ganesan}{Gan26} (\href{https://github.com/Naixu-Guo/quantum-open-problems/issues/140}{GitHub \#140}).

comment: For qutrits, let $p_{\mathrm c}(3)$ be the supremum of replacement probabilities with positive unassisted quantum capacity. The rank-two input gives $p_{\mathrm c}(3)\geq p_2(3)$, and antidegradability gives $p_{\mathrm c}(3)\leq3/8$. The exact threshold within those bounds and the regularized capacity in Eq.~\eqref{eq:h14-capacity} for finite $d\geq3$ remain open. Optimizing one use would still leave open what encodings across multiple uses can achieve. \sourcecite{ref:h14-ganesan}{Gan26} \sourcecite{ref:h14-emc}{EMC23}
